all_found.desc: [ADVISORY] The 'legacy ledger is a directory' case asserts only a nonzero exit from `state` in a harness with no runs, and resolveRun already fails there with ERR_NO_RUNS, so the assertion holds even if roots() ignored MigrateLegacyRows' error. A regression that silently swallows a ledger-migration failure passes CI.

[ADVISORY] StatusLines (plain `metareview status` FSM section) reads only the common-dir store, with neither the 0.13.x legacy fallback nor the migration. Right after upgrading, plain status prints 'fsm runs: none' while legacy runs exist, contradicting status --json's warning.

findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'legacy ledger is a directory' case asserts only a nonzero exit from `state` in a harness with no runs, and resolveRun already fails there with ERR_NO_RUNS, so the assertion holds even if roots() ignored MigrateLegacyRows' error. A regression that silently swallows a ledger-migration failure passes CI.

[ADVISORY] The legacy fallback in fromRunRunsDir and CLI migration via roots() are exercised only from the main checkout, never from a linked worktree, where the legacy store (main checkout's .metareview/runs) differs from the current worktree. Resolving the legacy location from the current worktree instead of RunStoreRoot would go undetected; linked-worktree upgraders would lose runs.

[ADVISORY] No test asserts the new Report.Warnings entry buildFor emits when LegacyRunsPending is true. If the warning is dropped or points at the wrong path, 0.13.x users get no hint and CI does not notice.

[ADVISORY] MigrateLegacyRuns moves every legacy run directory with no check of whether it is still live, so a 0.13.x binary still driving that run loses it mid-flight. With worktrees on different versions, the new binary moves the old binary's active run and the old binary's next fsm command fails with no such run.

[ADVISORY] A MigrateLegacyRuns error (e.g. EXDEV from os.Rename when the git common dir is on a different filesystem than the main checkout) is returned from roots() and aborts every fsm command, read-only ones included. Users with --separate-git-dir or split mounts find every fsm command failing on every invocation until they move .metareview/runs by hand.

[ADVISORY] LegacyRunsPending counts any non-dot directory in the legacy store, including collided ids and names failing ValidateRunID that the migration never moves, so the 'any fsm command migrates them' warning never clears and STORE_COLLISION repeats on every fsm command. After one collision or stray directory, status permanently shows a false warning and operators learn to ignore it.

[ADVISORY] StatusLines (plain `metareview status` FSM section) reads only the common-dir store, with neither the 0.13.x legacy fallback nor the migration. Right after upgrading, plain status prints 'fsm runs: none' while legacy runs exist, contradicting status --json's warning.

[ADVISORY] The architecture doc and the repo.StoreDir comment say the shared store exists in a bare repository, but ctxDeps.roots() still resolves storeRoot first and returns ERR_NOT_A_REPO for a bare main worktree. Bare-clone users are told it works while every fsm command refuses there; #174 is not fixed by this part.

[ADVISORY] The edited retention paragraph still says '`metareview status` lists the runs of the main worktree', but the scan is now scoped to the worktree containing each run's work_dir and SKILL.md says so. The two docs contradict each other; agents misread status from a linked worktree.

[ADVISORY] StoreDirIn is documented as the one definition of the store layout, yet the FSM writer side hardcodes the 'metareview' segment in several places and resolves the common dir with its own git call. Writer and readers agree only by convention, so a future layout change to one side silently splits them (#169's class).

findings.issue: The ledger row's fsmRunDir is now relative to git's common directory but the row only records repoRoot, so repoRoot+fsmRunDir names a nonexistent path.
